source.title: Detect and Suppress: A Mechanistic Defense against Adversarial Patches in VLA Models
source.authors: Yukiya Horiba; Koshiro Aoki; Shunsuke Yasuki; Bum Jun Kim; Taiki Miyanishi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE features and hidden-state intervention as tools for an adversarial defense, but does not test the superposition or polysemanticity claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports VLA SAE-feature correlations and the effects of suppressing a selected feature on task success. These results concern a VLA adversarial defense, not the geometry, capacity, or canonical status of features in the claim versions. The intervention and task-success results are recorded with versions ["none"]. Probe detection metrics are omitted because they evaluate the detector rather than feature geometry or superposition.
record.test_reason: The study uses a TopK SAE (1x expansion, so not even overcomplete) as a tool to find an attack-correlated feature in VLA models. It reports only its defense's task success and probe detection. Nothing it measures bears on superposition geometry, capacity, polysemanticity causes, LLM feature recovery, canonicity of SAE features, or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also stress that both selecting the feature and controlling intervention timing and strength matter, and that λ trades attack robustness against benign performance (Fig. 3).
record.recipe_differences: This is an SAE-based inference-time defense in VLA models, not a toy-network superposition experiment or a replication of the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention timing, intervention strength, patch type, and attack persistence change reported outcomes. Under intermittent UADA attacks, conditional intervention improves task success; continuous intervention can sharply degrade benign performance. Under persistent attacks, no intervention method improves success. Detector specificity also varies with the patch type used to train the probe.

fits_no_version.finding: A single SAE feature in π0.5 and SmolVLA correlates with adversarial patch presence. Suppressing it only when a probe fires raised intermittent-attack success (e.g. π0.5 n=10: 26.0→32.4). Continuous suppression degraded performance, and no method helped under persistent attacks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in VLA policies can track adversarial-patch presence and serve as conditional intervention targets, with benefits dependent on intervention timing and strength.

record.problems: The evidence is limited to two VLA models and LIBERO-10, with attacks evaluated in simulation. No uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are reported for the task-success results. The study itself notes modest gains and benign degradation for SmolVLA, and no recovery under persistent attacks.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcome rows were left out. Probe detection statistics and patch-type detector-specificity results were omitted because they assess the attack detector rather than feature geometry or superposition.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity transition, geometry: not studied.
Capacity competition and polysemantic neurons: not studied.
Non-capacity causes of polysemanticity: not studied.
Distributed features or SAE recovery in LLMs: not tested. The SAE is 1x expansion on VLA mean-pooled states, and reconstruction quality is not reported.
Completeness, stability, canonicity of SAE features: not tested.
One- vs multi-dimensional features: not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The SAE uses a 1x expansion ratio (latent dim = model dim), so it is not an overcomplete dictionary and offers no evidence about superposition. Rows are correctly linked to none. The omitted probe detection metrics (Tables 1, 5) and the λ sweep (Fig. 3) are defense evaluations and also bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test superposition, overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular feature geometry.
The study does not test capacity competition, polysemantic neurons, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
The study does not investigate alternative causes of polysemanticity.
The study concerns VLA models and does not test whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or recoverable as SAE features.
The study uses an SAE feature for intervention but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The study suppresses a decoder-direction contribution but does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.operation_detail: Compare the selected SAE feature with randomly sampled SAE features by patch-presence correlation and success rate under suppression

conditions.value: selected feature versus random features from layers deeper than detection layer

rows.measure: Mean Pearson correlation with patch presence and task success rate
rows.baseline: Random features; exact values not stated
rows.value: Text reports the selected feature had the highest correlation and highest success rate; some random features improved over baseline by smaller margins and others reduced success rate
rows.note: Exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: This compares feature-selection choices for the defense (selected vs random features), which is method tuning rather than a test of any version. The values are figure-only and not stated in the text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
